faqs.q: What is a scrub-jay, and why does it matter in Deltona?
faqs.a: The Florida scrub-jay is a federally Threatened, cooperatively breeding bird found only in Florida scrub — including Deltona's Lyonia Preserve, one of its strongholds. Jay families hold territories in the oak scrub of the preserve and remaining undeveloped parcels, and they are protected in every sense: no disturbance, no habitat clearing without federal process. For homeowners, jays matter as a planning fact on scrub lots and as a neighbor to enjoy — they are famously tame. Our role is identification and respect; jay habitat is never a service area.

faqs.q: Can you relocate a raccoon from my Edgewater attic?
faqs.a: Only on Florida's strict conditions. Under FWC Rule 68A-9.010, a live-captured native animal must be released or handled within 24 hours, and an off-site release is lawful only within the same county, on 40 or more contiguous acres, with the release landowner's written permission — or it can be released on-site once the home is sealed. Raccoons are Florida's most-reported rabies carrier, so we never promise a casual drop-off in the woods, and nonnative animals such as iguanas and Muscovy ducks may never be relocated at all.

Opossums and striped skunks work yards after dark, armadillos dig lawns and beds, eastern moles tunnel the sandy ground, and Brazilian free-tailed and evening bats roost in older rooflines through the warm months. The county's habitat — beach cities, inland St. Johns River towns, and the fast-growing Deltona corridor — and features such as St. Johns River, Blue Spring State Park, Tomoka State Park, Halifax River keep that pressure close to housing in every season.

Florida has no winter shutdown for this work, so Edgewater jobs run year-round, with the one hard legal gate being bats: exclusion is legal only from August 15 through April 15, and maternity-season bat calls become inspection and scheduling. Our crew works under FWC Rule 68A-9.010 with the property owner's authorization — Florida issues no nuisance-trapper license — checks any live trap at least every 24 hours, and seals the entry as part of the job so the next animal cannot use the same opening.
